subject.title: fix(compaction): retry loop can burn tokens when summarizer model is unavailable

question: Should staged compaction stop after a fixed number of generic fallback split summaries, and what threshold/fallback result should OpenClaw use when the summarizer is persistently unavailable?
rationale: Current main has the source-reproducible token-burn path, but the candidate fix trades token savings against potentially less complete session context during outages, so the cutoff policy is a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Land the typed staged breaker
options.body: Accept the open PR's typed generic-fallback tracking and two-consecutive-fallback cutoff after resolving conflicts and current checks.

options.title: Revise the cutoff policy
options.body: Ask the PR to change the threshold, fallback text, cooldown behavior, or partial-summary handling before merge.

options.title: Keep partial-summary behavior only
options.body: Reject the staged breaker and close the linked PR if maintainers decide repeated split attempts are preferable to earlier degraded summaries.

recommendation.title: Land the typed staged breaker
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR's typed generic-fallback tracking and two-consecutive-fallback cutoff after resolving conflicts and current checks.
